assumptions.summary: Positions rather than people are fixed nodes; people move and inherit rank, salary, relationships and time attributes.
Competence is represented by a normal variable centered at 0.5; initial satisfaction is 0.5.
ICM has 370 positions, seven ranks, 85% initial fill, external hiring for ranks 1-2 and an HR workload cap.
One tick is one month; annual churn counts leavers over 370, and training/recruitment costs follow source rules.
Prior satisfaction is strongest, work-group satisfaction is second, and supervisor/office peers are weaker influences.
Promotion raises satisfaction and a random threshold determines whether an employee quits.
Performance depends on competence, supervisor/group performance, company/group time and satisfaction.
The 80% full target and 25%/35% churn cases are paper scenarios, not calibrated organizational limits.

language_observations.summary: The reusable writing moves are phase decomposition, relation separation, proxy disclosure, timing-before-event-order, recurrence-after-influence-ranking, figure-to-mechanism reading, fixed-target tradeoff and named evidence boundaries.
the Summary turns an HR pressure into a three-phase model route: Move from recruitment and retention pressure to the hierarchical network, three model phases, HR outputs, and bounded recommendations.
a churn definition is followed by the representation and modeling task: Define annual churn, explain why a multilayer network is needed, and hand the reader to the fixed-position representation.

distinct organizational relations are separated before tensor integration: Keep hierarchy, work-group and office relations semantically distinct, show their edge patterns, and only then combine them in a tensor.

missing employee stability is handled by fixed positions and refreshed person attributes: Use positions as persistent nodes while people move and inherit rank, salary, relationships, and time attributes.
a behavioral timing premise becomes a monthly state-update order: Set a tick, queue HR work, count departures, apply costs, and refresh hiring or vacancy state in a declared order.

unavailable traits are disclosed before tractable proxies are used: State that competence or satisfaction cannot be directly observed, choose a bounded proxy or initial value, and name the resulting scope.
an influence ranking is explained before its satisfaction recurrence: Describe which person's satisfaction matters most, assign coefficients, constrain their sum, and pass the state to quitting.
promotion changes a local satisfaction state before downstream churn: Use promotion as a policy event, adjust the employee's satisfaction, then evaluate later leave decisions.
a uniform draw makes a leave decision inspectable: Generate a random value, compare it with a satisfaction-based threshold, and record the discrete leave event.

performance inputs hand a dynamic state to smart promotion: Combine competence, supervisor, group, tenure, and satisfaction terms, then choose a qualified high-performing predecessor for hiring or promotion.
a vacancy queue is interpreted through HR's explicit capacity ceiling: Relate current vacancies to the two-thirds workload and ten-percent company cap before making a staffing recommendation.
figures are read through a mechanism and a next check: Use budget, vacancy, fill, and churn plots to name the direction, the structural mechanism, and the data needed to reproduce it.

a fixed fill target keeps direct and structural consequences together: Hold 80% full status visible while reading HR capacity, recruitment, training, salary, vacancy compounding, and indirect stability.

a high-turnover middle layer is analyzed by rank-specific flows: Read supervisor and junior-manager churn, promotion, recruitment, and ending headcount separately before making a conditional HR claim.

recommendations are paired with named model weaknesses: Recommend HR expansion, satisfaction improvement, full-section placement, and performance promotion, then retain missing layers and unrealistic promotion behavior as limits.
future layers stop where data and representation stop: Propose friendship, workplace skills, position skillsets, and a people-following tree without presenting them as completed simulation evidence.

results_trace.summary: The source reports almost 86% positions filled over thirty years, with low recruitment cost and persistent training cost.
When vacancies exceed the 10% HR capacity, the source shows vacancy compounding and loss of the 80% full target.
The 25% and 35% churn cases are interpreted through fill status, vacancy structure and direct budget consequences rather than one scalar optimum.
Middle-manager churn is higher than other ranks in the source stress case, but the HR-health interpretation is conditional on small affected groups and promotion rules.
Recommendations are to expand HR, increase satisfaction, place new employees in fuller sections and use performance ratings for promotion.

source.title: Organizational Churn in Information Cooperative Manufacturing

source_quality.summary: All 17 physical pages were read twice and visually reviewed. The paper moves from organizational churn pressure through a tensor and fixed-position representation, three phased models, satisfaction and performance decisions, budget/vacancy scenarios, rank-specific stress, and recommendations bounded by future-work and representation limits.

decisions: how to represent fixed positions and relations, how to order monthly events, how to choose HR actions, and where data prevent generalization
inputs: 370-position hierarchical ICM, churn and recruitment pressure, rank/work-group/office relations, HR capacity and fill target
outputs: multilayer tensor, phased churn model, satisfaction/performance functions, hiring/quitting procedures, budget/fill scenarios and HR recommendations

title: Organizational Churn in Information Cooperative Manufacturing
unresolved_questions: The Summary's three-phase route and HR recommendations are outputs of a simulated ICM organization, not calibrated workforce evidence.
The tensor and fixed-position representation are inspectable, but complete node attributes, edge weights, time refresh rules, and source data are absent.
Competence, rank, salary, 370 positions, and a 0.5 satisfaction baseline are assumptions or proxies rather than observed employee records.
The two-thirds and ten-percent HR limits are source rules; vacancy simultaneity, queue ordering, capacity changes, and external validation are not supplied.
The annual churn and bookkeeping expressions omit seed, cost provenance, unit audit, and released monthly event traces.
The satisfaction recurrence and promotion adjustment are structurally clear, but coefficients, rank-specific terms, bounds, and calibration are incomplete.
The random quitting threshold lacks a seed, probability clipping convention, simultaneous-departure policy, and fairness review.
The performance function combines useful state inputs, yet the exact coefficients, normalization, training data, and ranking validation are unavailable.
Budget and churn figures show a near-86% fill and stable training cost in the source's thirty-year simulation, but raw runs and uncertainty are absent.
The 25% and 35% scenarios expose vacancy compounding and HR capacity pressure, but they are internal scenarios rather than a general 80% threshold.
The middle-manager stress case is conditional on rank-specific churn, promotion eligibility, and no-recruitment assumptions; employee health is not measured.
Recommendations to expand HR, increase satisfaction, fill full sections, and use performance ratings retain the source's fixed-position and simulated-state limits.
Friendship, skills, information, and a people-following tree are proposed future work; no new layer is simulated or validated.
The source admits that promotion into a supervisor role over empty positions may be unrealistic, so the model should not be generalized without a representation check.
